title: Efficient and Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Framework for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
one_liner: Pretrain a diffusion-based policy from offline data, distill it into a faster actor, and use uncertainty estimates plus shift detection to decide when online exploration is worth the risk.
lead: Offline-to-online reinforcement learning starts with a policy trained on a fixed dataset, then improves it with real interaction because the offline phase supplies a strong starting point before expensive online trials begin. The attraction is data efficiency: online learning starts from a competent policy instead of from scratch. The danger is distribution shift, meaning the states seen online can differ from the states covered by the offline data. Diffusion-based policies can represent complex action distributions, meaning weighted sets of plausible actions, but they are often slow to sample and they do not automatically say when they are uncertain. DUAL addresses both issues. In the offline phase it uses a diffusion planner to train a fast actor policy, meaning the network that outputs actions, and a transition model, meaning a predictor of the next state after an action. In the online phase it adds a Laplace approximation, meaning a local Gaussian approximation around learned weights, to estimate epistemic uncertainty, meaning uncertainty caused by limited knowledge rather than by random outcomes, and combines that with state-shift detection to decide how boldly the policy should explore.

problem.h2: Why offline-to-online RL needs speed and caution at the same time
paras: An offline policy can give online learning a good starting point, but that starting point is only reliable where the offline dataset has support. As soon as online interaction moves the agent into less familiar states, the policy can make confident but poor action choices.

Diffusion policies are attractive because they can model complicated action choices, yet repeated diffusion sampling can be slow during online control. A useful method therefore needs two things together: a faster way to act and a principled way to notice when the agent has stepped outside what the offline phase really taught it, because speed without caution causes unsupported actions and caution without speed makes online control impractical.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Distill a slow diffusion planner into a fast actor and guide its online updates with uncertainty and state-shift signals so exploration happens mainly when the offline policy is unreliable.

panels.title: 1. Learn from offline trajectories
panels.viz_args: Train a diffusion planner on the offline dataset so it captures many good action choices seen in past trajectories.
panels.caption: The offline phase learns a strong starting action model before any new interaction is spent.

panels.title: 2. Distill into a faster actor
panels.caption: The actor copies the diffusion planner's action knowledge while removing repeated sampling steps at runtime.

panels.title: 3. Estimate uncertainty
panels.viz_args: Use a Laplace approximation around the actor weights to measure how unstable the action prediction is under limited data support.
panels.caption: Uncertainty rises in parts of state space where the offline data gave weak evidence.

panels.title: 4. Detect transition-state shift
panels.caption: The algorithm checks whether the predicted next state is far from what the offline transition model expects.

panels.title: 5. Adapt online exploration
panels.caption: The agent explores more when knowledge is weak and exploits more when the distilled actor is supported by the offline data.

steps.text: Fit a diffusion-based policy on the offline dataset so the model learns a broad starting action model for the states covered by the dataset, because the online phase should begin with many plausible actions already encoded instead of discovering them from scratch.

steps.b: Distill the planner into a fast actor and transition model
steps.text: Train a simpler actor to imitate the planner's actions and train a next-state predictor alongside it, because online control cannot afford many reverse-diffusion steps at every decision.

steps.b: Estimate epistemic uncertainty from the actor
steps.text: Approximate uncertainty around the actor weights with a Laplace method so action uncertainty is larger where the offline training signal was weak or inconsistent.
Compare current online transitions to the offline transition model's expected behavior so the algorithm can detect when the agent has moved into a less familiar part of state space.

steps.b: Use both signals during online improvement
steps.text: Increase exploration or caution when uncertainty and shift are large, and trust exploitation more when both signals remain small.

paras: The paper changes the role of a diffusion policy in offline-to-online RL. Instead of using the full slow planner directly throughout online fine-tuning, it extracts a faster actor from that planner and then attaches uncertainty and shift-awareness to decide when the actor should be trusted, because the planner contains useful action knowledge but is too expensive to sample at every online step.
object.object: fast uncertainty-aware actor distilled from an offline diffusion planner

hidden.name: whether the current online state-action choice lies inside or outside the region where the offline policy has reliable support
paras: The agent never directly observes support coverage. It only sees states, rewards, and its own predictions. The important hidden quantity is whether the current decision is still backed by the offline dataset or whether the policy is now extrapolating.

DUAL estimates that quantity in two ways. Weight-based uncertainty asks how sensitive the action prediction is to plausible changes in the trained actor. Shift detection asks whether predicted transitions now look unlike the offline transition patterns. These signals complement each other because one is about model confidence and the other is about state coverage.

heat.caption: Dark cells mark the signals DUAL uses to decide when the fast actor should exploit and when it should probe for new information.

reads.html: Ask whether the policy is still acting in a part of the task that the offline data actually taught it well.
DUAL estimates support reliability through actor uncertainty and transition-state shift, then uses those estimates to regulate online exploration under offline-to-online distribution change.

mechanism.h2: Why distillation plus uncertainty is a good fit for offline-to-online RL
paras: Distillation matters because the diffusion planner contains useful action knowledge but is expensive to query repeatedly. Copying that knowledge into a faster actor preserves most of the offline phase's structure while making online control practical at every environment step because the actor can emit actions directly instead of running many reverse-diffusion updates first.

The Laplace approximation matters because it turns a single trained actor into a local uncertainty estimate around its learned weights. That estimate is not perfect, but it is informative where the actor has little evidence from the offline dataset. In those regions, small changes in plausible weights can change the chosen action more sharply.

Shift detection matters because an agent can be uncertain for two different reasons: the action mapping is weakly learned, or the current state is simply far from the offline data. The transition model gives a direct test for the second case. Combining the two signals lets the algorithm separate routine exploitation from the moments where online data collection should focus on unfamiliar states.

stages.s: Offline trajectories and a diffusion planner
Distill the planner into a fast actor and transition model
Estimate actor uncertainty with a Laplace approximation
Check transition-state shift during online interaction
Exploration and exploitation guided by speed plus caution

math.words: train the actor to match the distilled diffusion policy while carrying a penalty term that reflects uncertainty under the local weight approximation
symbols: the mismatch between the fast actor's action and the distilled diffusion planner's action
a term derived from the local weight covariance that grows when the actor is uncertain
the weight that controls how strongly uncertainty changes the actor update

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose two states have the same imitation error of 0.2 relative to the diffusion planner.
In the first state, the uncertainty penalty is 0.1 because nearby plausible actor weights choose similar actions.
In the second state, the uncertainty penalty is 0.7 because nearby plausible actor weights disagree strongly.
With beta set to 0.5, the first total loss is 0.25 and the second is 0.55.
The larger loss marks the second state as one where the actor should be treated with more caution during online adaptation.

math.note: The uncertainty term is a proxy for how weakly supported the actor's decision is under the offline training signal.

charts.title: Offline-to-online baseline without DUAL
charts.note: A slower or uncertainty-blind policy spends online interaction less carefully because it either acts too slowly or trusts unsupported actions too easily.

charts.title: DUAL
charts.note: The gains come from using the diffusion planner as an offline teacher, then using uncertainty and transition shift to decide when online exploration should override exploitation.

items.b: Distillation can lose important action diversity.
items.html: If the fast actor copies only the planner's average tendency, it may remove action modes that mattered for recovery or exploration in the full diffusion policy.

items.b: The uncertainty estimate can be poorly calibrated.
items.html: A local Gaussian weight approximation is only a local model of uncertainty. If the actor is far from locally quadratic behavior, the estimate can understate or overstate risk.

items.b: Shift detection depends on the transition model.
items.html: If the next-state predictor is weak, large transition error may reflect a poor model rather than a truly unfamiliar region of the online state distribution.

Check that distillation keeps policy quality high, validate uncertainty against held-out offline states, and use the transition model as one signal among several rather than as an unquestioned detector of unfamiliar states.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Choose a benchmark with an offline dataset and a costly online phase. Compare a slow diffusion-policy baseline, a distilled actor without uncertainty, and DUAL with both uncertainty and shift detection.

Measure decision latency, online return over interaction steps, and how often the exploration signal activates in unfamiliar states. The demo should show that DUAL works because the fast actor reuses offline knowledge while the uncertainty and shift signals prevent blind reuse outside the offline support region.
demo.closing: A convincing result is that online return rises quickly without spending many steps on reckless exploration, and that the exploration signal turns on mainly where the offline data were sparse.
